title: 1965 AHSME Problem 22
statement:
If \(a_2\ne0\) and \(r,\) \(s\) are the roots of \(a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2=0,\) then the equality

\[ \begin{aligned} a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2 &=a_0\left(1-\frac xr\right)\\ &\quad\cdot\left(1-\frac xs\right) \end{aligned} \]

holds:

solutions.text:
If \(a_0\ne0,\) then \(rs=\frac{a_0}{a_2}\ne0\) and \[ \begin{gathered} a_0\left(1-\frac xr\right) \left(1-\frac xs\right)\\ =\frac{a_0}{rs}(x-r)(x-s)\\ =a_2(x-r)(x-s), \end{gathered} \] which is the original polynomial for every \(x.\) If \(a_0=0,\) at least one denominator on the right is zero.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The right side requires both roots to be nonzero
Use \(rs=\frac{a_0}{a_2}\) to compare the leading coefficients
